name: Togolese Fetri Detsi
description: Fetri detsi, a deliberately, distinctively mucilaginous okra soup from the Ewe people of southern Togo, is genuinely built to be slippery - real technique finely chops the okra so it releases maximum sliminess, which is functional, not accidental: the real, traditional way to eat it is by hand, using the soup's own slickness to help swallow bites of fufu whole, not eaten with a spoon.

steps_detailed: Cook the okra in the palm oil with the jalapeño, 5-6 minutes, until it releases its real, sticky sliminess.
Add the ground crayfish, tuna, and a splash of water, and simmer 15-18 minutes until thickened and genuinely slippery - this real mucilaginous texture is the entire point, not a flaw.

name: Togolese Akume
description: Akume, a fermented cornmeal porridge, is genuinely more acidic and dense than a plain cornmeal porridge - real technique lets the cornmeal batter ferment before cooking, which is what gives akume its distinctive tang, closer to a Togolese polenta than to plain, unfermented pap.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal with 1 cup water and the vinegar into a thin batter.
Let ferment at room temperature 8-12 hours to develop real tang.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly, then reduce heat and simmer 12-15 minutes, beating often, until very thick and dense.

name: Togolese Fufu
description: Fufu, cassava and plantain pounded together into a smooth, stretchy dough, is genuinely central to Togolese communal dining - real technique takes two people working together, one pounding, one turning and moistening the mass, which is why it's traditionally a shared, social task.
steps_detailed: Boil the cassava and plantain together until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Pound vigorously until smooth and stretchy, adding a little water as needed to keep the right consistency.

name: Togolese Djenkoume
description: Djenkoume, tomato cornmeal cooked into a thick, polenta-like consistency, is a genuine Togolese specialty - real technique reserves a cup of the tomato base as a dipping sauce, then spoons the finished cornmeal into ramekins to hold its shape, unmolding it to serve warm alongside grilled chicken; it's not fried into patties.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion, garlic, and ginger in the palm oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and tomato paste, and simmer 12-15 minutes until a thick sauce forms.
Set aside about a cup of this tomato mixture to serve as a dipping sauce.
Pour the chicken broth into the remaining tomato mixture and bring to a boil.
Gradually whisk in the cornmeal, stirring constantly, and cook 10-12 minutes until very thick.
Spoon into small oiled ramekins, pressing smooth, then unmold onto plates and serve warm alongside the reserved sauce and grilled meat.

name: Togolese Gboma Dessi
description: Gboma dessi, a spinach and tomato stew, is a genuine Togolese everyday dish, real technique building a proper tomato base first before the greens go in.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 3-4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer 6-8 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter, add the spinach, and simmer 10-12 minutes until tender.

name: Togolese Ablo
description: Ablo, a soft, bouncy steamed rice cake, is a festive Togolese specialty, shared with neighboring Benin, real versions genuinely yeasted for a real rise.
steps_detailed: Blend the rice into a fine flour, then whisk with the cornmeal, sugar, and baking powder and enough water to form a thick, smooth batter.
Let rest 30-45 minutes.
Spoon into small greased molds and steam over simmering water 20-22 minutes until set and springy.

name: Togolese Groundnut Sauce
description: A rich groundnut sauce, shared across the wider West African region, real technique whisking the peanut butter slowly for a smooth broth.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter slowly with the tomatoes and a little water, add to the pot.
Simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender.

name: Togolese Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and ginger, reflecting Togo's Atlantic coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and ginger, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Togolese Fried Plantain
description: Fried ripe plantain, a common Togolese side dish, real versions using genuinely ripe plantain for real caramelization.
steps_detailed: Fry the plantain slices in a little oil, turning once, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply caramelized and golden.

description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Togolese home cooking.

Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Togolese Bissap
description: Bissap, a hibiscus drink, is a beloved Togolese beverage shared across much of West Africa.
steps_detailed: Warm the hibiscus tea and stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Chill and serve over ice.

name: Togolese Tomato Onion Sauce
description: A simple tomato-onion sauce base, used across many Togolese stews.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
